fit_notes: Envelope-encrypt-values-in-file pattern fits git-committed, long-lived site secrets, not a per-conversation, short-TTL model-boundary vault (no native TTL/audit).
BSD-3-Clause permits use as-is; a pure-Python re-implementation (X25519+ChaCha20Poly1305 via `cryptography`) is directly portable into a pure-Python, no-Rust package.
Confirmed by direct LICENSE fetch: Business Source License 1.11+, not OSI-approved, no copying; also requires an always-on Vault server, which conflicts with a no-always-on-service constraint.

Confirmed dual-licensed by direct LICENSE fetch, copying/import permitted with notice. `Fernet.decrypt(token, ttl=seconds)` implements exactly the kind of TTL check a short-lived pseudonymization vault needs, replacing bespoke AEAD+TTL logic.
GPL-3.0: no copying under a permissive, no-GPL policy. Transparent per-file git filter model does not match a runtime vault (per-conversation, TTL, audited reveal) anyway.
A commonly chosen component for PII detection and anonymization pipelines. MIT permits use/copy with notice.

MIT permits copying with notice. Its `Vault` class (placeholder<->value mapping object shared between Anonymize and Deanonymize scanners) is a close structural match for pseudonymization vault objects generally; worth porting the mapping-object shape, not the whole scanner pipeline where a detector is already chosen.

Apache-2.0 permits copying. Format-preserving encryption is a fallback idea only if a token kind needs to keep exact alphabet/length; bespoke partial-preserving rules per token kind (e.g. keeping a subnet or a domain RID) may already cover the need without copying code.

Licence would permit copying, but Puppet's `--noop` runs its own catalog/agent model (Ruby), incompatible with a stack that has already chosen DSC v3 as the declared source of truth for read-only drift checks. Nothing to replace.

Confirmed Apache-2.0 by direct LICENSE fetch (repo metadata reported NOASSERTION). Its read-only, no-enforcement design validates a test-mode-only, remediation-off rollout approach, but it is Ruby, not portable into a pure-Python package.
Confirms the Get/Test/Set DSC v3 pattern generally. MIT PowerShell resource code is out of scope for a Python-core tool; relevant only if that tool ever ships its own DSC resources.

Wrong domain (asset/licence tracking) and AGPL-3.0 forbids copying. No merge-key precedence documentation found.
